title: Anchor viewport on filter and reload changes
description:
[Spec ref] §4 last bullet (viewport keeps position relative to anchor row when filters change), §8 scroll-to-match centers row.
[Actions]
1. Viewport anchor: on visibility change keep top visible row identity, adjust scrollTop accordingly; table must not jump.
2. Scroll-to-row helper centers a given row in the viewport (used by search, fn filters).
3. Ensure programmatic scrolling never changes horizontal position (§4).
[Acceptance]
- Manual: with a filter toggled, the same anchor row stays at the same viewport position; scroll to row N centers it without horizontal drift.
design:
# qt7.3 — viewport anchor + selection remap: design (final)

Spec: §4 last bullet (filters change: selection preserved by line number;
viewport keeps its position relative to the anchor row — no jump), §8
(scroll-to-match centers the row). Resolution: `get_rows(offset, limit)` now
serves the visible sequence (dsq.3), and the visible sequence is monotonic in
line_no — so any line→visible-index query is resolvable in the UI WITHOUT new
IPC shapes, by binary search over 1-row probes (`get_rows(i, 1)`, ~log2(N)
round trips, each one row).

## New pure module `ui/src/viewportAnchoring.ts` (+ vitest)

```ts
interface Anchor { line: number; offsetPx: number }       // identity = 1-based line_no
captureAnchor(firstVisible: { index: number; line: number | null }, scrollTop: number): Anchor | null
resolveLineIndex(line: number, count: number, lineAt: (i: number) => Promise<number | null>): Promise<number | null>
  // binary search: first index whose line >= target; null only when target > last visible line
anchorScrollTop(index: number | null, anchor: Anchor, rowCount: number, viewportPx: number): number
  // index*ROW - anchor.offsetPx, clamped to [0, count*ROW - viewport]; null -> bottom
remapSelection(lineNos: number[], count: number, lineAt): Promise<number[]>
  // sorted resolve per target, nulls (hidden rows) keep the row selected - keep the entry as line-no
```

Anchor row hidden after the filter change: the binary search lands on the
nearest still-visible line AFTER it (the "nearest continuation" interpretation,
documented); none remaining -> scroll to the bottom.

## LogTable

- Live anchor ref: the existing scroll/render path stores the first virtual
  item's {index, line_no, offsetPx = vi.start - scrollTop} on every layout pass
  (rows not yet in the cache -> line null -> anchor null -> fallback: keep
  scrollTop as-is).
- `visibilityEpoch` layout effect (before the fetch effect): capture from the
  ref, resolve via lineAt (probes cached into the rows Map — valid for the new
  epoch; ChunkPlanner unaffected), set scrollTop only (§4: horizontal position
  untouched by any programmatic scroll — assert scrollLeft stays).
- `fileEpoch` keeps the full reset incl. scrollTop = 0 (§2). No new props.

## Selection remap by line number (§4 bullet) — console side

`uiConsole`: every visibility-mutating action (setLevel, addFilter,
toggleFilter, removeFilter, pins) with a non-empty selection first resolves the
selected indexes' line_nos against the CURRENT (pre-mutation) visible sequence
(cached rows or `get_rows(i, 1)`), sends the mutation, refetches the snapshot,
then binary-searches each line_no in the NEW sequence and dispatches
`{kind: "selection-remap", indexes}` (reducer: replaces selection.indexes,
keeps anchor behavior per selection.ts). Hidden rows keep their place in the
selection list as line-nos are not dropped (they simply do not resolve back;
store nothing for them — the visible-selection contract is about visible rows).
Empty selection: zero extra IPC.

## Text RPC for acceptance (rule 6)

TableHandle/console/`__headless` gain `viewport(): { scrollTop, scrollLeft,
anchor: {index, line} | null, anchorOffsetPx: number }` — assertions in tests
and e2e use this, never DOM poking.

## e2e (rule 4)

- State 17 `anchor-scrolled-refilter.mjs`: stub pre-filtered... stub loads, the
  state script scrolls, toggles a level off via __headless, asserts by numbers
  (viewport().anchor.line unchanged, anchorOffsetPx unchanged) AND commits a
  golden PNG of the held viewport.
- Existing states untouched unless goldens move.

## Not in this bead

- §8 search panel wiring (2wu.1) — only keeps using the same centering helper.
- Perf of probe calls (perf epic; a 20-row selection costs ~460 1-row probes).
acceptance_criteria: manual run: no viewport jump on filter change; centered scroll-to-row
notes:
Design fixed: binary-search resolution over get_rows 1-row probes (no new IPC), anchor ref pattern in LogTable, selection remap done console-side per visibility-mutation, viewport() RPC for assertions. Full text: docs/notes/qt73-design.md + bd design field.
Milestone 1+2: viewportAnchoring.ts + 17 module tests green; selection-remap in state.ts; console remap flow + viewport() RPC wired (all uiConsole/state tests green)
Progress: LogTable wiring done (anchor ref + restore effect + lineAt probes + resolved scrollToRow + viewport() handle), tsc clean; next: vitest + build + e2e state 17
Done: all gates green - vitest 125/125, build clean, e2e all states 0.000% + new golden anchor-scrolled-refilter, design oracle ok. Fixed en route: epoch-guard fetch loop + synchronous mirror clear (stale pre-refilter chunks polluted probe cache); lineAt probe epoch guard. Ready to close.
Live check (coordinator): 23/23 PASS x2 consecutive; anchor 649594@-252px held across level refilter, selection lineNos round-trip remap, centering constant, scrollLeft stable.

title: Core: visibility engine
description:
[Spec ref] §7 combined semantics; §11 counters; §12 pin override.
[Actions]
1. Engine state: filter list with per-filter on/off, level set enabled/disabled, category set enabled/disabled, pin list.
2. visible(i) = (no filters OR text match) AND level_on AND category_on OR pinned (§7 formula), evaluated over an index; produce a visible-rows view (sorted vec of line indexes) recomputed on any change.
3. Counters per level that ignore level toggles: count of rows which become visible if that level is enabled (shown on level buttons, §11).
4. Selection preserved by line number when visibility changes (§4 last bullet).
[Pseudocode]
struct Visibility { filters: Vec<(Matcher, bool)>, levels: EnumMap<Level, bool>, cats: HashSet, pins: Vec<Pin> }
fn recompute(&mut self) -> VisibleView
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests: OR over active filters, no filters = pass, level off hides, category off hides, pin makes hidden row visible, counters ignore level toggles.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core visibility green

title: Core: simple query language
description:
[Spec ref] §6 (grammar OR < AND < NOT, quoted terms, parentheses, case-insensitive keywords), plus span API for §9 highlight rendering.
[Actions]
1. Tokenizer: quoted terms, keywords AND/OR/NOT (case-insensitive), parentheses; everything else = syntax error.
2. Recursive-descent parser: parse(text) -> Result<Query, SyntaxError>; precedence NOT > AND > OR.
3. Evaluator: eval(query, line_text) -> bool (case-insensitive over full line text).
4. Span API: positive_positions(query, line_text) -> Vec<Range> for every occurrence of every positive term (NOT terms excluded) - reused by highlights.
5. Syntax error -> criterion matches nothing; app never panics.
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests for spec examples: error AND timeout; NOT info; (auth OR login) AND failed; precedence a OR b AND c == a OR (b AND c); unclosed quote / empty term / stray symbol -> no match, no panic; multi-occurrence spans correct.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core simple_query green

title: Core: plain, line-number and regex match modes

3. Regex: compile case-insensitive; regex crate fast path, fancy-regex fallback for lookarounds/backreferences (Python-compatible syntax per spec); invalid pattern compiles to NeverMatch, never panics (§5).
4. LineNo: exact 1-based match.
[Acceptance]

title: Core: row parsing (formats A/B)
description:
[Spec ref] §3 parse rules and all edge cases; §3.1 level names.
[Actions]
1. Parse into Row { line_no (1-based), time_display (HH:MM:SS.mmm; for format A strip date part before T), category, level, message, raw }.
2. Whitespace separators (sequences of spaces), first field is timestamp.
3. Format A: field 2 = category, field 3 = level candidate. Format B: field 2 (elapsed) discarded, field 3 = level candidate, field 4 = category.
4. Level recognition: long names (LOG_*) and short codes crt/err/wrn/msg/dbg/trc, case-insensitive; unrecognized candidate = MSG level, candidate and rest = message. Missing level = MSG.
5. Categories: missing / single-field = uncategorized; two-field line = uncategorized, MSG, second field is message; empty line = empty message, uncategorized, MSG.
6. Levels enum: CRITICAL, ERROR, WARNING, MSG, DEBUG, TRACE (§3.1).
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests cover: full A line with and without level tag, full B line, category missing, two-field line, single-field, empty line, multiple-space separators, short and long level codes, unknown level candidate treated as message.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core parsing green; every §3 edge case has a named test

title: Core: scanner - line index and format detection
description:
[Spec ref] §3 (auto-detect two formats by first non-empty line), §16 (hundreds of MB feel instant).
[Actions]
1. Reader over mmap: enumerate line offsets (memchr on b'\n'), build u64 offset index (Vec<u64>).
2. Auto-detect format A (KSIVA) vs B (PLAIN) from first non-empty line; B = 5 fields starting with HH:MM:SS.mmm.
3. Empty/blank-only file handled gracefully (zero rows, empty state stays).
4. Expose: line_count(), raw_line(i) (bytes without trailing newline), detected_format().
[Pseudocode]
struct Scanner { data: Mmap, offsets: Vec<u64> }
fn detect_format(first_line: &[u8]) -> Format
[Acceptance]
- Unit tests with small fixture files written in-test (spec sample lines) for both formats.
- Integration: scan test_logs/log.txt (175 MB) in < 2 s on dev machine; line_count matches wc -l.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p logviewer-core scanner; scan 175 MB log.txt under 2 s both formats detected

title: get_rows/search walk the full file for §11 counts they discard
description:
[Spec ref] §11; docs/BENCHMARKS.md visibility section; sampler evidence in log_viewer2-vdr notes.
[Context] ensure_visible_cache's valid-cache branch runs level_counts_excluding_levels (a full 1.29M-line walk in debug seconds) on EVERY read; get_rows_inner and search_visible_inner discard the returned counts, so every 1-row probe (lineAt, ~21 per remap binary search) costs a full walk — the live-debug 100% CPU spin after a run: sampled main thread inside get_rows_inner -> ensure_visible_cache +136 -> level_counts_excluding_levels for minutes at "idle".
[Actions] 1. Add a walk counter to VisibilityState (test seam); 2. RED test: a second get_rows on a valid cache must not increment it, snapshot must still report §11 counts with a cached sequence; 3. Split ensure_visible_cache: no-counts path for get_rows/search, counts walk only for visibility_snapshot; 4. Re-run the live spin probe: idle CPU after a heavy live run.
[Acceptance] cargo test walk counter green; sampled idle logviewer (after a live run) shows no continuous get_rows walks; live_check fail profile unchanged.
notes: Accepted: walks-counter test green (reads on a valid cache cost zero walks; the snapshot keeps its counts walk); idle logviewer after a heavy live run at 0.0% CPU (was ~100% for minutes); e1/e3/e6 anchor checks that failed deterministically at HEAD now PASS — the plateau was the per-probe walk latency; live run 51/51. Commit f111643.

design:
# q1f.1 — pins UI: design (final)

Spec: §12 (pin = rule in modes p/pr/ps/pn N; pinned rows always visible
overriding filters/levels/categories §7; Pinned tab like the Filters tab;
context-menu Unpin; §2.1 — a reload clears ALL pins), §10.1 (tab layout),
§4 (menu items Pin/Unpin present by selection coverage).

## Backend (landed already, bindings regenerarated)

- `load_file_inner` clears all pins on reload (tests: reload_clears_pins...,
  clear_pins_clears_all_and_invalidates).
- New RAW command `clear_pins` (the future :rmp; no panel button — §10.1
  shows no clear-all control).

## Console actions

- `pinSelected()` → one add_pin("lineno", "<line>") per selected row, inside
  ONE mutating critical section (single snapshot refetch at the end — the
  2wu.1 lesson). `unpinSelected()` → remove_pin(id) for every EXACT-ROW pin
  whose line number is among the selected rows' line numbers; `clearAllPins()` →
  clear_pins. Headless mirrors + snapshot (pins already in the snapshot).

## Menu semantics (documented interpretation)

- §4 presence: Pin is available when at least one selected row is NOT pinned;
  Unpin when at least one selected row is pinned.
- Pinned-ness evaluation UI-side from the snapshot's pin list: exact-row pins
  (lineno mode) cover their parsed line numbers; broad pins (plain/regex)
  cover rows whose cached raw text they match; simple pins are NOT evaluated
  (the simple engine is Rust-side) — they neither enable Unpin nor count a
  row pinned **for the menu's presence logic** (documented limitation).
- Unpin removes ONLY exact-row pins covering the selection. Rows pinned by a
  broad rule stay pinned (removal goes through the panel delete button —
  §12 says per-one removal via panel; the menu deliberately never nukes a
  rule matching an unknown number of rows).

## Panels

- Pinned tab mirrors FiltersTab anatomy (checkbox, command text with the
  :p-/-:pn- prefixes via the same canonicalizer shape, delete ✕, dimmed off).
- Replace the placeholder in SidePanel; Highlights keeps its placeholder
  (exx.2).

## e2e

- Golden: Pinned tab with entries + a disabled one.
- Golden: pins survive filter narrowing — a filter that hides everything
  except matched rows, pinned rows still visible (§7/§12 override), then
  context-menu unpin on a pinned row -> it disappears (if not filter-matched).
- Context-menu goldens with live Pin/Unpin items may re-baseline 14-selection-menu.
- §4: reload via __headless.clearAllPins equivalent — reload clears pins:
  assert pins empty after a reload-driven snapshot.

## Gates

Full gates from ui/; live-check section (h) by the coordinator at the
milestone; design oracle after any visual change.

design:
# exx.2 — highlights: design (final)

Spec: §9 (auto palette color rotation over a 10-color palette, semi-transparent
rectangles behind matched text, Message column only, overlapping rules,
per-rule checkbox/delete, color change via the SYSTEM color picker, rmh
later-but-command-now, highlights SURVIVE reload §2.1), §10.1 (tab item with
a color dot instead of the command prefix).

## Core (landed at exx.1, do not modify)

`HighlightEngine`: rules Pattern{matcher} / LineNo{line_no}, color_index
round-robin 0..PALETTE_SIZE, `row_spans(message) -> Vec<(start, len)>` byte
ranges in the MESSAGE text. Palette HEXES live in the UI layer.

## Shell (Rust agent)

- New managed `HighlightState`: core engine + parallel meta
  `Vec<HighlightMeta { mode, pattern, enabled, override_color: Option<String> }>`.
  Persists across `load_file` (§2.1 the OPPOSITE of pins — no reset).
- Commands (specta): `add_highlight(mode, pattern)` (rotation assigned by the
  core; unknown mode → Err in the dsq.3 style), `remove_highlight(id)`,
  `set_highlight_enabled(id, on)`, `set_highlight_color(id, hex)`
  (hex = CSS "#rrggbb" or null to reset to the palette rotation color),
  `clear_highlights()` (the future :rmh).
- `get_rows` RowDto gains `spans: Vec<SpanDto>`; spans are computed per row
  from the engine (cheap: only active rules) — byte offsets in the MESSAGE
  text.

## RAW shapes

```ts
SpanDto { start: number; len: number; color_index: number; override_color: string | null }
HighlightDto { id: number; mode: string; pattern: string; enabled: boolean; color_index: number; override_color: string | null }
```

`RowDto` gains `spans: SpanDto[]` (additive). Byte→JS string index conversion
happens ONCE in ipcClient (single normalization point).

## UI (second agent)

- Palette table `HIGHLIGHT_HEX: string[10]` from docs/UI_DESIGN.html tokens
  (§3.1); the resolved span color = `override_color ?? HIGHLIGHT_HEX[color_index]`.
- Highlights tab: checkbox, command text (:h :hr :hs :hn via the filtersTab
  canonicalizer shape), color dot (click → `<input type="color">`, the
  webview's system picker), delete ✕, dimmed off. Replaces the placeholder;
  rmh is NOT a tab button (§10.1 shows none).
- LogTable Message cell: overlapped semi-transparent rectangles behind the
  matched ranges (opacity from the design reference); level colors stay
  underneath (§9).
- Snapshot gains `highlights`; headless RPC: addHighlight, setHighlightEnabled,
  setHighlightColor, removeHighlight, clearHighlights.

## e2e + interpretations documented

- Goldens: two overlapping highlights (Message-only tinting), a disabled
  one (dimmed, no spans), a user-picked color dot; the hn whole-line case.
- Interpretation: an invalid pattern → never-match rule (renders nothing but
  keeps the slot), matching add_filter behavior.
- Interpretation: color rotation continues from the current engine counter
  across removals (core behavior; no re-indexing of existing rules).

title: Search panel and navigation
description:
[Spec ref] §8 (Ctrl+F opens, Chrome-style panel: input, Regex/Simple exclusive tumblers, match counter like match k of N or 0 / 0, prev/next buttons, close, cyclic navigation, search only over visible rows, start from current selection downward, scroll to match centered in viewport, Esc closes, arrows navigate matches while panel open and act as table navigation when closed), §14, §16.

design:
# 2wu.1 — search panel: design (final)

Spec: §8 (Ctrl+F; Chrome-style top panel: input, mutually exclusive Regex |
Simple tumblers (both off = substring), match counter «k of N» / «0 of 0»,
prev/next, close; cyclic navigation; over VISIBLE rows only; starts from the
current selection downward; scroll-to-match centers; Esc closes; arrows
navigate matches while open, act as row navigation when closed).

## Raw IPC (new, one command — Rust agent)

```
search_visible(mode: string, pattern: string) -> SearchMatchDto
SearchMatchDto { total: u32, positions: Vec<u32> }   // 0-based VISIBLE indexes, ascending
```

- mode ∈ plain | regex | simple (same strings as add_filter). Unknown mode →
  Err (dsq.3 precedent). Invalid pattern → matches nothing (core never()).
- Empty pattern → `{ total: 0, positions: [] }` («0 of 0»).
- Case-insensitivity comes from the core matchers.
- Scope: the shell's cached visible sequence (§7) — hidden rows never match.
- No cap on `positions`; the UI debounces recompute (250 ms). If that becomes
  slow on the big corpus, 7no.1 measures and decides.

## UI (reducer slice + console + components)

- `search { open, mode, query, positions, current }`; counter = (k, N):
  k = 1-based rank of the current match, N = total; «0 of 0» when N == 0.
- Actions: `openSearch` (Ctrl+F; focuses the input), `closeSearch` (Esc),
  `setSearchMode(m|null)` (exclusive tumblers), `setSearchQuery(q)` (debounced
  recompute → console action), `nextMatch(dir)` (cyclic; selects the match row
  + scrollToRow centering via the qt7.3 helper). Each recompute keeps the
  starting rule: first match at-or-below the selection's visible index.
- Global keydown: Ctrl/Cmd+F opens (file loaded only); while the panel is
  open Up/Down = match navigation; while closed Up/Down = select previous /
  next visible row (clamp at the edges — spec interpretation: «обычная
  навигация»), preserving shift/ctrl modifiers? No: plain arrows only move
  the selection, modifiers keep the §4 semantics through onRowClick paths.
- Selecting a match dispatches the ordinary selection events (the match row
  becomes the selection; multi-select untouched — §4 rule for the click kind).
- Panel markup per docs/UI_DESIGN.html (top-edge floating bar, compact
  tumblers, counter, ↑/↓/✕). Classes/tokens verbatim from the reference.

## e2e + gates

- States: open panel with a query (counter + highlighted row), regex mode,
  simple mode, cyclic wrap (0→last), search with a category hidden (N counts
  visible only). Committed goldens + numbers via __headless
  (search slice in ConsoleSnapshot; actions mirrored).
- Full gates from ui/, oracle from root; live-check section (g) by the
  coordinator at the milestone.

## Interpretations documented in code

- Both tumblers off = substring; tumblers are radio-like (turning one on
  turns the other off), clicking an active tumbler turns it back off? No —
  at least plain must remain: clicking an active tumbler switches to plain
  (both-off state). UI never sends an unknown mode.
- Arrows while the panel is open AND the focus is in a text field still
  navigate matches (the panel owns arrows while open).

title: Live check e1/e3/e6: refilter anchor settles at a transient plateau on 1M+ files
description:
[Spec ref] docs/PIPELINE.md para 5 (live window); docs/notes/2wu1-frontend-design.md (anchor rules).
[Context] Live checks on test_logs/log.txt (1,294,246 lines, debug build) fail deterministically at HEAD (reproduced twice in a row, identical numbers):
e1 (line 1->649594 offset 0->-252), e3 (line 649594 offset -252 vs stale a0=1/off 0), e6 (both scrollToRow settles captured the same line B+2471; deltas 5306/9874). Data is internally consistent with state().anchor lagging the serialized op queue: the settle heuristic (3 equal reads over 2.1s in debug load) converges to a transient plateau before the queued anchor recompute lands. g3 once read three zeros the same way (nondeterministic; passed in the baseline run).
[Actions] 1. Reproduce the anchor plateau with a focused probe (scrollToRow + poll state().anchor vs the queue's settle signal); 2. Decide: does __headless need an ops-queue settle signal the driver can await instead of the equal-reads heuristic; 3. Fix the settle (or the anchor reporting) and re-baseline the e-section; 4. Make g3's afterQuery use the same signal.
[Acceptance] `node scripts/live_check.mjs test_logs/log.txt` exits 0 (3 e-checks and g3 deterministic PASS) twice in a row; no suite regressions.
design: resolution: log_viewer2-7c3 — the e1/e3/e6 plateau was the ensure_visible_cache counts walk on every read: a settle's stable-3-reads converged on transient states while probes walked the full file. The walk-free read path (commit f111643) removed the latency; the anchor checks pass deterministically (live 51/51). No ops-queue settle signal needed.

title: Driver: investigate 100% Condvar spin and single-instance enforcement
description: [Spec ref] docs/PIPELINE.md para 5. [Context] After load-heavy live runs the debug driver thread spins in Condvar::wait_timeout (100% CPU) while idle; concurrent app instances raced the shared port file and made probes nondeterministic. [Actions] 1. Reproduce the spin, find the re-check loop defect in driver.rs wait_timeout path (likely recomputed zero timeout); 2. Single-instance guard (lockfile or kill-stale on startup); 3. Consider raising the 60s eval deadline or returning eval-failure as a first-class response. [Acceptance] Driver at 0% CPU in idle after a heavy live run; a second app start is refused or replaces cleanly; live checks pass twice in a row.
design: Three fixes shipped (commit 3b03d01): (1) single-instance flock on $TMPDIR/logviewer.lock taken in run() before any window — a second start exits 3 with a message; the OS releases on kill -9, verified live (second binary refused while the dev app ran) + unit test instance_lock_refuses_a_second_holder. (2) evalJs no longer retries a possibly-mutating snippet: a lost report is a first-class failure (a retry re-executed loads/filters/pins and doubled whole mutation batches — the identified amplifier). (3) request() has socket timeouts (3s per waitForApp probe, 300s otherwise). The 100% Condvar-spin sampler evidence resolved as the back-to-back ensure_visible_cache recomputes from mid-burst partial caches (bead 3af's bulk kills the mid-burst window); the driver wait loop itself was correct. Live: driver probes deterministic across runs (same fail profile before/after the change); the e1/e3/e6 plateau is pre-existing HEAD debt — bead log_viewer2-ddp. Residual: the 240s eval deadline stays; a queued-op drain/flush protocol is a larger protocol change, deferred unless ddp needs it.
notes:
Accepted: single-instance flock refuses the second start (exit 3, verified live); evalJs mutation retry removed, socket timeouts added; idle CPU after a heavy live run 0.0% x3 (the spin's root cause was the get_rows counts walk — bead 7c3); live checks green twice in a row. Commit 3b03d01.
Original evidence (sampler): the 100% CPU spin was NOT the driver wait — it was the tokio/main path in ensure_visible_cache -> level_counts_excluding_levels -> visible_with_counts, i.e. BACK-TO-BACK full recomputes of 1.29M-row passes for minutes. Amplifier identified: evalJs's transport retry re-EXECUTED mutating snippets (filters/pins/loads) whose first run merely lost its report, so one lost eval doubled the whole mutation batch and its loads/refetches; a lost report itself stalled the driver for the full 240s slot (the Node client had no socket timeout either). Fix directions: (1) evalJs retry only for read-only evals or an idempotency token; (2) socket timeouts + a queued-op drain/flush protocol; (3) single-instance + port-file ownership — all shipped in 3b03d01 (+ the sampled walk cause in f111643).

title: Harden visibility reads against mid-burst cache rebuilds
description: [Spec ref] S7; docs/BENCHMARKS.md visibility section. [Context] Audit (rhl.2 dsq.3 lineage): a read command (get_rows/search/snapshot) whose ensure_visible_cache lands between two set_category_enabled calls of a console burst rebuilds and caches a transiently partial whitelist state; a 1.29M-row scan holds the vis mutex seconds, so the burst queues behind it and the partial total is returned legitimately (epoch cannot reject it). [Actions] Option A: bulk set_categories_bulk(differential) with one invalidation; Option B: visibility-cache generation number returned in read DTOs so the UI attributes staleness. [Acceptance] A live-driver probe through the f1/f2 category burst returns the final-epoch totals on every read (no partial-cache scans observable); all suites green.
design: Option A chosen over Option B (generation numbers in read DTOs): the bulk command removes the window instead of tagging it, one IPC command instead of DTO churn and a UI attribution rule. set_categories_bulk(disable[], enable[]) applies the differential under ONE vis-mutex hold with one invalidation (disable first, then enable — the propagateToggle order). toggleCategory/setAllCategories call it; the Rust unit test asserts bulk end-state == sequential application plus the post-bulk read totals. Gates: cargo 35 + 123, clippy 0, vitest 349, e2e goldens 0.000%, typecheck clean. Live: f1/f2 burst PASS on the 1.29M-row test_logs/log.txt in two live runs (2026-11-24); identical e1/e3/e6 anchor fails existed at HEAD before the change (bead log_viewer2-ddp, control run documented).
notes: Accepted: f1/f2 category-burst live probes returned final-epoch totals in three live runs on test_logs/log.txt (1,294,246 lines); the final run fully green (live 51/51, 2026-11-25). Suites: cargo 36+123, clippy 0, vitest 349, e2e goldens 0.000%. Commit 084a796.
